source.citation: Thompson, D'Arcy W. (1917). On Growth and Form. Cambridge University Press. Chapter XV, 'On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures', pp. 652-669 (egg section pp. 652-660; sea-urchin corollary pp. 661-669, Figs. 328-330).
source.related_thompson_note: Thompson, D.W. (1908) 'On the Shapes of Eggs, and the Causes which determine them', Nature 78:111-113 (4 June 1908) - the egg section is 'in part reprinted' from it (p. 654 footnote).

claim.text: Birds' (and other hard-shelled) eggs are solids of revolution whose meridian curves form a definite, species-varying family of ovoids, comparable geometrically across species.

decomposition.C1_solid_of_revolution: The egg is a simple solid of revolution generated by a plane (meridian) curve (p. 652).
decomposition.C2_definite_family: The meridian curves constitute a definite family of ovoids running from the sphere (owl, tortoise) through ellipsoids with symmetrical ends (grebe, cormorant, pelican), 'cylindrical' forms (megapodes, sand-grouse), the common ovoid (hen), to blunt-pointed conical forms (guillemot, puffin, sandpiper, plover, curlew) (p. 652).
decomposition.C3_species_varying: The form is species-specific: 'the specific form ... of the egg' (p. 652); the named species occupy characteristic positions in the family.
decomposition.C4_comparable_across_species: Because every egg is generated by a plane curve of one family, eggs of different species can be compared geometrically (one coordinate system, one set of shape parameters).
decomposition.C5_prolate_never_oblate: 'the egg, while often pointed, is never flattened or discoidal; it is a prolate, but never an oblate, spheroid' (p. 652) => Elongation L/B >= 1 for all eggs.
decomposition.C6_steiner_oval_fails: Footnote p. 654: Jacob Steiner's Cartesian oval r + m r' = c, proposed as a general formula for all eggs, 'fails in such a case as the guillemot' and 'is purely empirical, and has no mechanical foundation'.
decomposition.C7_relative_size_asymmetry: Statement (5), p. 655: 'those eggs which are most unsymmetrical, or most tapered off posteriorly, are also eggs of a large size relatively to the parent bird' (guillemot, curlews, sandpipers, phalaropes, terns); the apteryx is the conspicuous exception (p. 656).
decomposition.C8_envelope_equation: p. 658: the egg (extensible membrane + incompressible fluid under external pressure) obeys p_n + T (1/r + 1/r') = P; 'the equation of all eggs in the universe' when generalised to p_n + T/r + T'/r' = P (p. 659).

mathematical_model.coordinate_system: Axis of revolution = x, normalised so the egg occupies x in [-1, 1] (half-length = 1, length L = 2 units). Meridian half-breadth y(x) >= 0; the egg surface is the surface of revolution of y about the x-axis. Physical scale: multiply by L/2 (mm).

meridian_family.name: Preston (1953) four-parameter ovoid family (also Todd & Smart 1984); the quantitative descriptor of Thompson's 'definite family' adopted from Biggins, Thompson & Birkhead (2018), who showed it is the most accurate of the published egg equations.

state_variables.x: normalised axial coordinate (pointed end at x = +1 by the Biggins convention when c1 < 0)

parameters.c0: overall breadth (c0 = half-breadth at the mid-point x = 0)
parameters.c1: odd (asymmetry) term - sign sets which pole is blunt
parameters.c2: even term - cylindrical (c2 < 0) vs biconical (c2 > 0) mid-body
parameters.c3: odd cubic term - pointedness of one pole

meridian_family.boundary_conditions: y(-1) = y(1) = 0 (closed poles); y > 0 on (-1, 1); near a pole y^2 ~ 2 R (1 -/+ x) so each pole is locally spherical with radius R = p(+/-1)^2 where p(x) = c0 + c1 x + c2 x^2 + c3 x^3.

special_cases.prolate_ellipsoid: c1 = c2 = c3 = 0, 0 < c0 < 1  =>  y^2 / c0^2 + x^2 = 1 (grebe, pelican: symmetric ends)
special_cases.ovoid: c1 or c3 != 0 (hen); pointed/conical when |c1| + |c3| large (guillemot, plover)
special_cases.oblate_spheroid_excluded: c0 > 1 would give B > L; never observed (Thompson's prolate-never-oblate)

meridian_family.fitting_method_biggins2018: Each egg photograph is segmented; the upper and lower outline y-values are divided by sqrt(1 - x^2) and regressed on {1, x, x^2, x^3} with weights (1 - x^2) (Gegenbauer lambda = 3/2 orthogonal basis in Analysis.R); residual error reported as fitPreston = mean squared residual / 4 on the half-length scale.

shape_indices.Elongation: E = L / B = 2 / (2 * y(x*)) = 1 / y(x*) where x* is the root of y'(x) = 0 (Biggins 'Elongation'; Thompson's spherical <-> E ~ 1).
shape_indices.Pointedness: fraction of the length lying between the widest point and the pointed pole: Pt = (1 - x*) / 2 (Biggins 'Pointedness'); 0.5 for symmetric ends.
shape_indices.PolarAsymmetry: ratio of the radii of the osculating circles at the two poles, larger / smaller: PA = max(p(-1)^2 / p(1)^2, p(1)^2 / p(-1)^2). Closed form derived here; it reproduces Biggins' numerically searched 'PolarAsymmetry' column on all 1389 eggs with Pearson r = 0.99997 and median ratio 1.000007.
shape_indices.Volume: V = pi (L/2)^3 * Integral_{-1}^{1} p(x)^2 (1 - x^2) dx (exact polynomial integral: the solid of revolution).
shape_indices.Axisymmetry_residual: RMS difference between the upper and lower half-profiles of a horizontal egg photograph, in units of half-breadth; ~0 iff the egg is a solid of revolution (tests C1).

thompson_mechanics.envelope_equation: p_n + T (1/r + 1/r') = P  (Thompson p. 658), i.e. T * 2H = P - p_n with H the mean curvature of the meridian surface, T the membrane tension, P the internal fluid pressure, p_n the normal component of external (oviduct) pressure.
thompson_mechanics.cone_equilibrium: A cylinder with conical ends of semi-angles theta, theta' stays in equilibrium in the tube, apart from friction, if p cos^2(theta) = p' cos^2(theta'); 'at the more tapered end where theta is small p is small' (p. 657).
thompson_mechanics.pole_relations: At a pole r = r' = R so (P - p_pole) R = 2 T. Uniform p_n => constant H => sphere (spherical egg, p. 659). With p_n = 0 at both poles and one T: R_blunt / R_point = (P - p_point) / (P - p_blunt) = 1, so asymmetric poles REQUIRE either different pole pressures or different pole tensions T_blunt / T_point = R_blunt / R_point > 1.
thompson_mechanics.derived_remark: Thompson writes (p. 659) that with p_n vanishing at the poles 'the tension T is greatest at and near the small end of the egg'. From his own equation P R = 2 T at each pole (p_n = 0), T_pole = P R_pole / 2 is proportional to the pole radius, so the tension is greatest at the BLUNT end; the small end has the smaller tension. We record this as a sign inconsistency in Thompson's side-remark, not in the claim under test.
thompson_mechanics.closure_of_the_family_by_curvature_const: Given the two pole curvatures 2/R_+ , 2/R_- (set by P - p at the poles), the equatorial mean curvature 2H_eq (set by P - p at the equator) and the volume V, the four Preston coefficients are determined (4 equations, 4 unknowns). This 'Thompson closure' is the forward model used in the script: ramping the pole pressure contrast from 0 produces sphere -> ovoid -> conical egg within the Preston family.

normalised_preston_coefficients_publishe.thompson_class: apteryx: relatively huge yet not markedly unsymmetrical (p. 656)
guillemot: blunt one end, characteristically pointed the other

biggins2018_main_dataset_species_means.note: 1389 eggs, 14 auk + 16 penguin species; Elongation mean +/- sd, Pointedness mean, PolarAsymmetry mean (computed from biggins2018_data_for_comparing_indices.csv).

biggins2018_goodness_of_fit_132_eggs.note: cf.* columns in biggins2018_comparison_of_fits.csv are mean-squared-error ratios (model / Preston).

deeming2018_outline_pcs_181_species.axes_identification_this_loop: PC1 correlates with log egg mass (Spearman rho = -0.356, p = 9e-7) and separates owls/doves/chaffinch (high, rounder) from albatross/gannet/goose (low, elongated) => elongation axis (sign: + = rounder). PC2 separates waders (Vanellus, Gallinago, Recurvirostra, Himantopus; high) from pelican/doves/swan (low) => asymmetry axis (+ = more asymmetric).
deeming2018_outline_pcs_181_species.thompson_statement_5_test: Spearman rho(PC2, egg mass / female body mass) = 0.391, p = 6.7e-8 (n = 181): relative egg size predicts asymmetry, as Thompson stated.

apteryx_exception.comment: relatively enormous egg with near-zero asymmetry, exactly Thompson's named exception (p. 656)

empirical_claims_to_test.test: Preston family RMS residual over breadth on published 132-egg fit table and on segmented specimens; Cartesian-oval negative control on the guillemot
empirical_claims_to_test.pass_if: median residual < 0.01 and Cartesian oval residual on C126 > 3x Preston residual

empirical_claims_to_test.test: between-species eta^2 and Kruskal-Wallis of Elongation, Pointedness, PolarAsymmetry (30 species) and order-level eta^2 of Deeming PC1/PC2
normalised morphospace; Thompson's named forms recovered from photographs fall in the published species ranges
empirical_claims_to_test.pass_if: owl E < grebe E < guillemot E and owl PA < grebe PA < plover/guillemot PA

empirical_claims_to_test.test: Thompson closure reproduces the Preston family; uniform pressure -> sphere; pole-tension sign
empirical_claims_to_test.pass_if: closure residual < 1e-6; sphere recovered; T_blunt > T_point under P R = 2T
